mechanism_narrative: The observed consistent week-over-week recovery in RETAIL_REC mobility over the last four weeks indicates a sustained upward trend that will continue, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean of the last 28 days, indicating a reversal or stagnation of the recovery trend.

mechanism_narrative: The significant recent surge in PARKS mobility, particularly the 14.1 point increase from t-1w to t-0w, signals a strong increase in outdoor activity and public comfort, which will spill over into and drive higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days, despite PARKS mobility continuing its upward trend or remaining significantly elevated.

mechanism_narrative: As WORKPLACES mobility slowly recovers and RESIDENTIAL mobility steadily declines, it indicates a collective shift back to out-of-home activities and routines, which will drive an increase in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines or stagnates over the next 14 days, even if WORKPLACES continues to rise and RESIDENTIAL continues to fall.

mechanism_narrative: The broad-based and sustained increase across multiple mobility categories (RETAIL_REC, GROCERY_PHARM, TRANSIT, WORKPLACES) suggests an underlying easing of local restrictions or increased public confidence in safety measures, which will continue to boost RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: Local policy announcements indicate a tightening of restrictions, or the observed upward trend in these mobility categories reverses, leading to no increase in RETAIL_REC.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent week-over-week improvement in TRANSIT mobility reflects increasing comfort with public transportation, directly supporting a short-term increase in RETAIL_REC over the next week as more people commute and travel for leisure.
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility declines or plateaus in the next week, and RETAIL_REC does not increase over the same period.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in RESIDENTIAL mobility below 14.0 percent change from baseline indicates a strong shift towards out-of-home activities and a return to pre-pandemic routines, which will directly translate to higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 14.0 percent change from baseline
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below 14.0 percent, but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The combined effect of increasing PARKS mobility (suggesting warmer, more favorable weather) and decreasing RESIDENTIAL mobility (people leaving homes) will drive a sustained increase in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as seasonal factors encourage outdoor and leisure spending.
failure_condition: If weather patterns become unusually cold or wet, reversing the PARKS trend, and RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The broad-based recovery across RETAIL_REC, GROCERY_PHARM, and WORKPLACES, all showing consistent week-on-week improvements, indicates a general economic and social reopening momentum that will continue to lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If any of the proxy series (RETAIL_REC, GROCERY_PHARM, WORKPLACES) show a significant decline over the next four weeks, contradicting the observed reopening momentum, and RETAIL_REC does not increase.
